None. This reel makes no datable claims (no model versions, prices, or
"as of" phrasing). The 58-year-old case is explicitly labeled illustrative in
the narration itself; no fact-check exposure.

## Verdict — authored from body

The scaffolder verdict (`artifactLines: ["Key finding one/two/three"]`) is a
canonical placeholder (verdict_audit.py's first pattern). The body carries
12 beats and ~475 words — well over the verdict-authoring threshold. Authored
four lines from the body's own nouns:

- "PET reads glucose metabolism, not malignancy" (B05, B12)
- "False positives: infection, healing wounds, brown fat, immune activation" (B06, B10)
- "False negatives: low-glycolytic tumors (thyroid, some prostate, mucinous)" (B07)
- "Imaging suggests — biopsy confirms" (B08, B12)

Narration rewritten to speak these findings aloud (was empty).

## BHTF exercise — authored

Old `command` was the canonical `[X]`-in-brackets scaffolder template
("Take what you learned from [Why a Glowing PET Scan Doesn't Actually Show
Cancer] and apply it to your own work…"). Replaced with a real, scaffolded
exercise built from the reel's own subject — the proxy-vs-thing distinction:
name a diagnostic tool you rely on, name the proxy it measures, list three
false-positive causes and one false-negative condition.

## Lens moves earned (LENS-NOTES.md)

- **Plato (artifact / world / relationship)** — the reel names all three
  explicitly: the artifact is the PET signal, the world is the tissue biology,
  the relationship is a proxy (B08, B12, verdict).
- **Popper (falsifiability)** — B10 is the reveal that falsifies the "bright
  = cancer" reading via biopsy. State-in-advance is met: the imaging report
  itself says "consistent with", not "confirms" (B08).
- **Hume (confidence is a property of the model)** — the whole reel is a
  Hume-style warning that the correlation glucose-metabolism ↔ cancer is not
  the mechanism.

Three moves earned; requirement was two.
